title: C10 DayLog v2 — the day-log fetch over C2 v1 slots (storage -> continuum)
description: The rendered segment/block day-log for one training window, served by GET /training/daylog?user_id=&window_id=. VERSION 2 (DP rebuild; D-R6 with D-R5, drafted 2026-08-05, awaiting founder ratification — plan: services/data-processing/docs/refactor_dp_service.md §5; renderer built at rebuild Stage E): the renderer walks C2 v1 content.slots instead of per-kind records — slots.caption -> Scene lines, slots.ocr -> World text (OCR) lines, slots.transcript -> speaker-bucketed transcript lines via its splits[]. Dedup key: latest updated_at per (chunk_id), rowid tiebreak — one record per chunk (Slot Law L2) collapses v1's (chunk_id, content.kind, discriminator) key, and updated_at replaces ingest_time as the axis (D-R5: created_at = first landing of a record_id, updated_at bumps only when record_json byte-compares different, so a no-op redelivery never re-windows a record while a heal flows into the next window). Training-window membership moves to updated_at with it. daylog_format_version and recipe_id bump at the transition; continuum's stamp-refusal (built, F3) is the safety net. The raw range read GET /context/records?user_id=&from=&to= is NOT retired and remains first-class. WIRE STATUS: v1 remains the running read until the Stage F cutover; nothing serves v2 before then — this file exists now because contracts precede fan-out (ORG.md), so rebuild Stage E builds and validates against it.

window_id.description: The training window this day-log renders. OPAQUE, path-safe, lexicographically ordered, derived from the window's END instant in UTC and minted in exactly one place. THE LENGTH BOUNDS ARE NOT REDUNDANT WITH THE PATTERN: in the Python validator this contract is enforced by, `$` also matches just BEFORE A TRAILING NEWLINE, so `w20260722T035900Z\n` satisfies the regex alone -- and that string is a different filesystem path from the id it looks like. Storage's own validator closes the same hole by using fullmatch rather than match; pinning the width to exactly 17 closes it here, and states the fixed-width property the lexicographic-ordering guarantee rests on. Consumers may rely on < / >= and on NOTHING else — it is not parsed back into a date, because under a [last_trained_t, now-delta) window there is no local date to name (a window can span 23 h, 25 h or 47 h). It is a PER-USER token, which is why user_id rides beside it here and on every window-addressing surface.

t_start.description: The window's lower bound on storage's UPDATED_AT axis (v2; was ingest_time in v1 — D-R5), RFC3339 UTC, inclusive. NOTE what this is not: the extent of the rendered content. Membership is by updated_at, so a chunk captured Tuesday and uploaded — or healed to a byte-different record — on Friday belongs to Friday's window and renders in a block anchored to Tuesday; segment/block timestamps can and do precede this value.

t_end.description: The window's upper bound on the updated_at axis, RFC3339 UTC, exclusive. Sits `delta` behind the wall clock at open time so an in-flight write cannot be assigned an updated_at below it yet commit after materialization read the range.

daylog_format_version.description: The renderer + row shape this body was produced under. Distinct from `version` (the contract's) and from `recipe_id` (the consolidation recipe's): it bumps when the segment/block shape or the rendered block text changes, and a bump re-materializes every cached day-log rather than serving an old dialect. It BUMPS at the v1 -> v2 transition (slot-walk renderer), which is what makes continuum's stamp-refusal the transition safety net rather than a formality.

recipe_id.description: The consolidation recipe whose `corpus` knobs (segment_seconds, block_segments) shaped this day-log. GLOBAL and versioned (recipe_id == filename stem in the C13 registry), never per-user — a per-user recipe id would fork the id per user and destroy artifact comparability. The gate policy is a SEPARATE artifact with its own id and is deliberately not here. Bumps at the v1 -> v2 transition alongside daylog_format_version.

home_tz.description: THE FALLBACK ZONE ACTUALLY USED when a record carried no device_tz — the user's C12 home_tz at materialization time. Recorded on the body because that is what makes a wrong-timezone adapter falsifiable after the fact (the D17 follow-up this field closes). It is NOT the zone every block rendered in: a block prefers the capturing device's own device_tz, so a travelling user's blocks carry different zones and different local dates within one day-log.

segments.description: Segment rows, ascending by t_start. One row per ~segment_seconds bucket on a GLOBAL epoch grid (floor(t_start / segment_seconds)) — not relative to the window start, which would go negative once membership is on a storage-clock axis, and which would also make a bucket depend on which window happened to collect it. Sources are C2 v1 slots of the deduped record set: latest updated_at per (chunk_id), rowid tiebreak.

seg_id.description: `{window_id}_s{ordinal:05d}` where ordinal is the row's position in this array. The ORDINAL, not the epoch bucket index — the latter is a nine-digit number at 10 s buckets. Regenerated per window; nothing persists it.

caption.description: Visual caption texts whose record t_start fell in this bucket — C2 v1 slots.caption.value (v2 routing; was content.kind caption|text in v1).

asr.description: Speech lines whose t_start fell in this bucket — C2 v1 slots.transcript.splits[] (v2 routing): one entry PER SPLIT, each bucketed by the split's own t_start rather than the parent chunk's, so a 30 s chunk's speech is anchored where it was said. A record whose dialect attempted speaker_align but whose transcript slot is a hole contributes nothing here (L11: a hole is a failure, and the renderer never fabricates from a slot the record does not carry).

spk.description: The split's aligned speaker label (slots.transcript.splits[].speaker); null where alignment found no turn.

ocr.description: World-text reads whose record t_start fell in this bucket — C2 v1 slots.ocr.value (v2 routing). An empty-string value (the honest empty claim: OCR ran, no legible text) contributes no line; an absent slot (a hole) likewise contributes nothing — the two are distinguishable in the record, not in the day-log.

quality.description: Segment quality score, or null == NOT SCORED. C2 v1 carries no quality field, so this is null throughout v2; unscored is not the same as zero and must never be treated as failing the amplification gate.

tz.description: The IANA zone the CAPTURING DEVICE reported for this bucket (C2 source.device_tz, first contributing record wins — a ~10 s bucket cannot straddle a real zone change). null when no contributing record carried one, which is what makes the renderer fall back to home_tz.

blocks.description: Scene blocks: runs of TEMPORALLY ADJACENT non-empty segments (gap > 6*segment_seconds starts a new block, and a block holds at most block_segments segments). Adjacency is what keeps a late-uploaded backlog honest — it is temporally distant from today's capture, so it forms its own blocks with its own anchors rather than being welded onto them.

block_id.description: `{window_id}_b{ordinal:04d}`. Regenerated per window; nothing persists it.

seg_ids.description: The seg_ids this block was rendered from, in order.

text.description: The rendered block: an anchor line (`On <local-date>, around <HH:MM>-<HH:MM> local time:`) followed by the optional `Scene: `, `Heard: ` and `World text (OCR): ` lines — the line labels are UNCHANGED from v1 (D20: the block text is contract, and the v2 re-baseline is the differential proof re-run at Stage E WP-E4, not a label change). THE ANCHOR IS IN THE TEXT, never metadata-only, because this string is what the model trains on. Wall-clock readings are in the block's own zone — pairing a local date with UTC clock readings would anchor a moment up to a day away from the event.

anchors.description: The anchors woven into `text`, exposed structurally too. Open to additive keys (a `place` filled in once geo enrichment lands).

date.description: The block's LOCAL date in the zone it rendered in — which is the device's zone when it reported one, so two blocks in one day-log can legitimately carry different dates.

place.description: Null in v2; no geo slot exists in the v1 slot set (world-data enrichment remains deferred).

quality.description: min() over the block's SCORED segments, or null when none is scored. The amplification quality gate lives in continuum, not here: the day log keeps everything and low-quality rows are excluded from training, never from the record.

content_fingerprint.description: A stable content hash over (window_id, user_id, segments, blocks). Computed BY WHOEVER RENDERS and only ever compared to ITSELF across runs — it is continuum's day-log stage key, not a cross-backend equality claim. At the v1 -> v2 renderer transition it changes once and that night re-runs, which is correct: the input genuinely changed.
